uncertain.note: sic: 'Preniierement' for 'Premierement'; after 'Pre' a two-legged n with one arch, then two dotted i's (both readers, 8x). Wrong sort, as printed.

uncertain.text: Cuerre leur frere, & mari de ladite de
uncertain.note: sic: 'Cuerre' for 'Guerre'; a plain capital C with no bar or spur (both readers). As printed.

uncertain.text: ont dõnce deux des beaux-freres dudit
uncertain.note: sic: 'dõnce' for 'dõnee'. At 5x the fourth letter is an open c with no crossbar, the fifth an e with a full bar (body-4.jpg, line 2). Wrong sort, as printed.

uncertain.text: des peres, meres, enfans, freres & ſeurs, beaux fils, & be-
uncertain.note: 'desperes' is set tight in the print with a round (word-final) s; separated as two words per conventions §1.

uncertain.text: prouuer vne ehoſe, en laquelle la foy des parens ſeroit
uncertain.note: sic: 'ehoſe' for 'choſe'. At 10x (body-5.jpg, line 7, x~300-520) both the last letter of 'vne' and the first of 'ehoſe' have the closed eye and crossbar of an e; the c/e transposition reader A saw ('vnc ehoſe') is not in the print. Wrong sort, as printed.

uncertain.text: le parent ne ſeroit point produit par la partie parente
uncertain.note: the a of 'partie' is a damaged or under-inked sort (top curl detached from the bowl); read as a from bowl, foot and width (both readers).

uncertain.text: roit aux parẽs & ne nuiroit à perſonne: comme'quand
uncertain.note: 'parẽs': a long horizontal nasal bar over the e (5x), not the short rising acute of 'parenté'. 'comme'quand' sic: a comma-shaped sort at apostrophe height stands between 'comme' and 'quand' with no word space (body-6.jpg, line 8, x~1330); it prints like the apostrophes of 'qu'en' and 'd'vn' and is transcribed as printed, though the sense wants plain 'comme quand' (foul case or a filler that rose).

the mark between 'l' and 'parentes' is a small solid round dot printed at ascender height, not on the baseline (margin-2.jpg x~400, y~1085, checked at 14x); it is dot-shaped, not comma-shaped, so not an apostrophe sort. Read as the point of the abbreviation 'l.' printed high (a turned or high-riding point sort); but notes b and c print the same abbreviation as bare 'l etiam', so 'l parentes.' with a stray sort is possible. Pointer for a human: margin-2.jpg, first line of note a.
a short raised word-break stroke after 'pre', same sort as after 'ma' and 'pro' in note b; transcribed as a hyphen.

sic: the sort before the point is the italic fount's curled-top t (as in 'parentes' and 'tut.'), with no descender; an italic z in this fount (compare 'ſoubz' on p057) has a flat top and a tail below the baseline. Read 'alleguét.' as printed although the sense wants 'alleguéz' / 'alleguées'. Checked at 14x (margin-3.jpg y~575).

the smallest and faintest line on the page; at 7x the three sorts before the first point read a, u, d ('aud.'); 'ead.' is not supported by the first sort, which has the bowl and stem of an a. The note prints below the last body line; beside_line is the nearest line above it.

beside_line values: the margin is crowded and the notes drift; notes a-c begin level with the line carrying their marker (b level with 'l'aage…', c with 'le parent…', checked on margin-3.jpg), note d five lines below its marker, note e below the last body line.
